answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so an identity’s influence depends on reachable, independently attested paths rather than claimed accounts. A sybil cluster may add many nodes, but if its external cut is sparse, its conductance is low; few walks escape it within the bound. Under normalized voting and limited seed mass, this bottleneck limits the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, whether its identities are named nectar, basalt, or dawn.
